site.all_your_cameras_in: All your cameras in a single video.
site.cam_ui_joins_several: cam-ui joins several USB cameras and two microphones into one synchronized mosaic. Record it to MP4 or use it as a camera in your video calls.
site.free_no_ads_first: Free, no ads. The first run also downloads ffmpeg (about 100 MB). Needs Windows 10 or 11.
site.this_demo_uses_generated: This demo uses generated images, not real cameras. In the program each tile is one of your cameras, and the layout adapts to their shape.
site.they_rarely_agree_on: They rarely agree on resolution, frame rate or timing. cam-ui checks what each one really delivers and keeps image and sound together.
site.every_camera_microphone_shares: Every camera and microphone shares one clock, so picture and sound stay aligned even when each device starts at a different time. The «Sync» button turns any phone into a clapperboard: it flashes a never-repeating code, like a barcode in time, in front of each camera, and cam-ui measures to the millisecond how late each one arrives and sets its delay by itself.
site.each_output_channel_comes: Each output channel comes from any microphone, and from its left, right or mixed input, with its own gain. Live level meters.
site.flip_rotate_crop_zoom: Flip, rotate, crop and zoom each camera. Adjust brightness and colour while recording, without stopping. Each camera remembers its settings and its place in the mosaic, even if it stays unplugged for months.
site.reads_which_sizes_frame: Reads which sizes and frame rates each camera offers and tests which ones it can keep up with. If a camera rejects a mode, cam-ui tries another by itself.
site.records_mkv_converts_mp4: Records to MKV and converts to MP4 at the end, so a crash does not lose the video. The preview never stops while recording.
site.offers_mosaic_as_camera: Offers the mosaic as a camera in Teams, Zoom or Meet. Needs OBS Studio installed (free; you do not need to open it). Video only, no audio.
site.watch_with_microphone_listen: Watch (and, with a microphone, listen to) the mosaic live from another PC or phone on the same wifi, in a browser, with fullscreen, no app needed. Works at the same time as recording and the virtual camera; view only, no password.
site.if_camera_stays_locked: If a camera stays locked by a stuck ffmpeg, F12 closes them all and starts again.
site.normal_everything_set_up: Normal. Everything to set up: cameras, layout, framing, colour, audio and output. Screenshot with test cameras.
site.compact_just_preview_main: Compact. Just the preview and the main buttons. It can stay on top of other windows while you work.
site.mini_one_thin_bar: Mini. One thin bar with Record and Stop, no preview. Esc goes back to the normal window. All three sizes are also in the tray icon menu.
site.one_small_file_cam: One small file, cam-ui-instalar.cmd. You can read it in the repository before running it.
site.sets_up_its_own: It sets up its own Python (you don't need Python installed) and downloads ffmpeg. The first time takes a couple of minutes.
site.use_from_start_menu: Use it from the Start menu
site.cam_ui_opens_when: cam-ui opens when it finishes. To update, run the installer again: your settings stay.
site.with_python_3_10: With Python 3.10 or newer and ffmpeg.exe next to camui.py:
site.what_does_installer_put: What does the installer put on my computer?
site.everything_goes_into_your: Everything goes into your own user folders (the program in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\cam-ui, its own Python and ffmpeg in %LOCALAPPDATA%\cam-ui), with a shortcut in the Start menu and on the desktop, and it shows up in “Installed apps”. It does not touch any Python you already have, or ask for administrator rights.
site.from_windows_settings_apps: From Windows Settings → Apps → Installed apps, look for “cam-ui” — same as removing any other program. It asks whether to also delete your captures, recordings and settings, or keep them for next time.
site.why_does_windows_warn: Why does Windows warn me about the file?
site.installer_is_plain_script: The installer is a plain script that is not signed by a company, so Windows shows a warning for any downloaded script. If you want to check it first, open it with a text editor: it is short and only downloads the files listed above.
site.how_much_space_does: How much space does it need?
site.about_500_mb_free: About 500 MB free on the drive where your user folder lives (usually C:), for Python, ffmpeg and the libraries; the installer warns you if it finds less. If that drive is too full, you can install on another one: open a command window, type set CAMUI_INSTALL_DIR=D:\cam-ui (with the drive and folder you want) and run the installer from that same window.
site.does_virtual_camera_need: Does the virtual camera need something else?
site.yes_obs_studio_installed: Yes: OBS Studio installed (free, obsproject.com). cam-ui uses its virtual camera, so you pick “OBS Virtual Camera” in your video-call app. Only one program can use that camera at a time, so do not start the virtual camera inside OBS at the same time.
site.my_camera_shows_low: My camera shows low quality or fails to open
site.in_framing_tab_press: In the Framing tab press “Detect” and then “Test modes”. cam-ui measures what each mode really delivers and picks the best one that works. If it still fails, send me the report (see the next section).
site.default_since_pack_45: The default since pack 45 (it can be turned off in Settings → Advanced). Each camera opens on its own and all at the same time, and none of them holds back the others: a slow camera, one that drops out, or another PC's, only stutters or shows “No signal” itself — the rest stay smooth — and it comes back on its own. Restarting the mosaic or starting to record no longer reopens the cameras. If you chain another PC running cam-ui and both use the new engine, its camera lines up with yours by the time it was captured, even if the two PCs' clocks don't match. If something works worse than with the usual engine (a single ffmpeg for all cameras), untick it.
site.does_keep_working_with: Does it keep working with the PC locked?
site.yes_locking_win_l: Yes. Locking (Win+L) doesn't stop desktop programs, and while the preview is running (and with it recording, “On the network” and the virtual camera) cam-ui asks Windows not to put the computer to sleep for inactivity; the screen still turns off as usual. What Windows doesn't let any program prevent: putting it to sleep on purpose (closing the lid, the power button, Start → Sleep — the lid action can be changed in Windows' power options) and, on laptops on battery with “Modern Standby”, sleep arriving anyway a few minutes later. Plugged in, it can run for as long as you want.
site.can_i_use_my: Can I use my phone as one of the cameras?
site.yes_two_ways_simplest: Yes, two ways. The simplest, nothing to install: the phone-camera server is always on (nothing to turn on first) — in the Settings tab, under “Phone camera”, open any of the fixed addresses it shows, all ending in /movil (with no port number when the PC's port 443 is free, e.g. https://192.168.1.129/movil), in the phone's own browser. That page just asks for camera permission to scan a QR code — by itself it doesn't add anything. As soon as you grant it, a one-time QR code appears on the PC's own screen — in a pop-up window, right away, whichever tab you're on — scan it with that same phone camera (still on the /add page) and the phone navigates on its own to the capture page — the camera appears on its own in the list, already ticked and ready to record. Because you have to be looking at the PC's screen to see that QR, nobody else on the wifi can add a camera without you seeing it happen. If you already have the “watch over the network” page open on the phone, there's a shortcut button there too — “Add phone camera” — that jumps straight to this same /add address, so you don't have to remember a second port. The first time, the browser will warn the connection “isn't private”: that's cam-ui's own one-off certificate (needed for the browser to allow the camera at all), not a fault — “Advanced → Continue” once and it's remembered; on an iPhone or iPad there's one extra, one-time step too (an “Install certificate” button in that same tab, with its own QR code — open that page in Safari: Chrome and other iPhone/iPad browsers only download it as a file), because Safari won't allow the camera there at all without it — Android needs none of this. Video only for now, no audio. The phone is remembered once it pairs, so it won't need the QR again even after restarting cam-ui — Settings has a “Manage mobile devices” list to see which ones (“iPad”, “iPhone” or “Android · model”, with their last connection), rename them or forget any of them. The older way still works too: install an app that streams video (such as “IP Webcam”), put the phone on the same wifi, and in cam-ui press “Add network camera…” with the address the app shows (something like http://192.168.1.50:8080/video, or an rtsp:// address) — useful if you'd rather keep that app's own settings, or already have it set up. Either way, you can double-click the camera later in the list to edit its name without losing its framing or colour settings, and if it drops the connection cam-ui doesn't stop the whole mosaic: it shows “No signal: <name>” in that camera's spot, keeps recording the rest, and reconnects on its own once it comes back. The same “Add network camera…” box also accepts another PC's cam-ui “watch over the network” address, to chain several computers together — it arrives with the same shape and frame rate as that PC's mosaic (its framing included, no added black bars, up to 30 fps); its “Over the network” size setting is only the maximum, so pick a bigger one there for more resolution.
site.can_i_watch_from: Can I watch it from another PC or phone?
site.yes_in_mode_menu: Yes: in the “Mode” menu (or the button bar, the Settings tab, or the tray icon) turn on “Over the network”, and open the address it shows (something like http://192.168.1.50:8554/) in a browser on another device on the same wifi — clicking that address in the status bar opens it for you in your own default browser, as a quick check. The page has a fullscreen button, and if a microphone is set up, a “Turn on sound” button (browsers block audio from starting on its own) with its own mute and volume controls. It's view only — anyone on your wifi can open that address while it's on, there's no password — and it keeps working while you record and while the virtual camera is on. The first time, Windows may ask to allow cam-ui through the Firewall: allow it, or no device will be able to connect.
site.can_i_send_chromecast: Can I send it to a Chromecast or AirPlay?
site.chromecast_yes_two_ways: To a Chromecast, yes, two ways. From the computer running cam-ui: with “Over the network” on, press “Open in VLC” (Settings tab, “Mode” menu, or tray icon) — if VLC is installed, it opens the stream there instead of the browser, and from VLC's own Playback → Renderer menu you can pick a Chromecast on the same wifi; VLC does the conversion itself, nothing else to set up in cam-ui. If VLC isn't installed, it offers to open its download page. From whoever's watching in a browser: the viewer page itself has a Chromecast button — on Chrome or Edge with internet, it's the real native cast icon (the YouTube one): one tap, pick the TV, done; cam-ui switches on a second, separate ffmpeg just for that (H.264 over HLS, live, only while it's actually being watched on the TV — the regular browser view keeps using the same low-latency stream as always). Without that icon (no internet, or another browser), it falls back to a button that explains how to use the browser's own “Cast…” feature instead — either way there's always something that works. AirPlay has no equivalent on Windows: no player brings it built in the way VLC brings Chromecast (AirPlay video only really exists as a macOS feature), so it isn't supported for now.
site.yes_cam_ui_checks: Yes. cam-ui checks for a newer version when it opens and, if there is one, asks before installing it (you can turn this off and check by hand with the “🔄 Updates” button or the tray icon). There's also an optional “update automatically when opening, without asking” tickbox, for whoever prefers not to be asked at all. Either way it keeps a copy of the version you had and the program can go back to it with one click; your configuration is never touched.
site.is_worth_writing_even: It is worth writing even if everything worked. It tells me which cameras and setups to look after.
site.what_you_used_for: What you used it for, which cameras you have, what you liked and what cost you.
site.camera_will_not_open: A camera will not open, the video comes out wrong, the program closes.
site.tell_me_what_you: Tell me what you are trying to do and I will look at how to make it possible.
site.you_need_free_github: You need a free GitHub account. To report a problem, attach the camui.log file (next to camui.py; the “Registro” button opens it) and, if it is about resolution or frame rate, the “Test modes” report. You can also read what others have sent.
site.cam_ui_is_free: cam-ui is free and has no ads. If it saves you time, buy me a coffee and help me keep improving it.
